newsitem.title: INDIA: India Escorts 96/97 net 1.27 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India Escorts 96/97 net 1.27 bln rupees.

text.p: Indian tractor and motorcycles makers Escorts Ltd on Monday announced a 1996/97 (April-March) profit of 1.27 billion rupees against 1.00 billion rupees in the previous year.
The company set a dividend of 45 percent, up from 40 percent in the previous year.
"The increased dividend is payable on capital enhanced from 593.8 million rupees to 651.6 million, arising from the conversion of equity warrants into shares," the company said in a statement.

"The higher dividend was approved by the board of directors at its meeting held today on reviewing business prospects of sustained profitability improvement in the future years, and the comfortable liquidity available after provisioning for investments."
Escorts said its earnings per share in 1996/97 were 19.52 rupees. The company gave no comparative figure for the previous year.
"Our 10 percent return on sales is well above the prevailing trend in the engineering industry as a whole," the firm said. It did not immediately give sales figures.
The firm is in the process of building a tractor manufacturing plant near the western Indian city of Pune costing 1.75 billion rupees, funded by internal resources.
The company also expects "substantial dividends" on its investments in the cellular telephony business, the statement quoting Escorts chairman Rajan Nanda as saying.
